intents.answer:
Juice Up (Coral Springs): 7-day rebrand plus owned Stripe checkout on juiceupeats.com instead of marketplace handoffs at pay. The owner reported roughly ~20% higher online pickup revenue after that shift (scope: digital pickup on owned surfaces).

Native apps on Google Play and the App Store share menu, Stripe, and kitchen tickets. In-app tiered loyalty replaced a legacy rewards path; the owner described roughly ~25% growth in the digital revenue base as repeat guests moved onto owned ordering.

Daniel was lead product designer and design engineer: brand, checkout/catering flows, and mobile UX.

intents.answer:
Juice Up catering on the owned site: packs and bulk ordering stay on juiceupeats.com with the same Stripe path as pickup — no marketplace handoff at checkout.

Flows emphasize clear pack sizing, pickup scheduling, and kitchen-ticket handoff so back-of-house sees one order stream.
followUps: What changed in the checkout funnel?

intents.answer:
On the Juice Up case study page, mobile no longer uses a touch carousel for hero shots — react-slick’s handlers were blocking vertical page scroll on iOS/Android.

Below the `md` breakpoint the study uses a static stacked image list; desktop keeps the carousel. Tradeoff: less swipe flair on small screens for reliable scrolling.

The problem was high-intent guests leaving juiceupeats.com for Toast, DoorDash, or Uber Eats at “Order Now.” The fix kept menu → cart → embedded Stripe → confirmation and kitchen tickets on one surface.

Design choices: shallow navigation, clear category cards, guest checkout with pickup scheduling, and counter-ready order numbers on confirmation.

Allied Credit Union (Mahalo): mobile banking redesign with tiered authentication (passcode, biometrics, security questions) and clearer member journeys.

Daniel contributed competitive audit, core flows, and member journey UX. The case study frames tradeoffs explicitly: e.g. offering “Use passcode instead” at key steps to reduce abandonment vs. strict single-path login.
followUps: How do you mitigate auth friction?

intents.answer:
Maia / HRIT: AI-native GovTech HR talent platform in AWS GovCloud (FedRAMP context). Work included modular design systems, conversational workflows for matching and recruitment, and role-based, multi-tenant interfaces.

Patterns: structured guardrails behind the LLM, progressive disclosure on SmartMatch-style recommendations, and separating automation from human hiring decisions.

URC Records: 0→1 e-commerce for an underground dance vinyl label. Focus on collectors who already know what they want: fast storefront, BPM/key metadata, simple email/password auth via Supabase, Stripe checkout, and inventory accuracy with webhooks.

Daniel Fornica is a product designer across B2C, B2B, and SaaS, often operating as lead product designer and design engineer: brand and UI/UX through flows that ship (React, design systems, owned checkout, mobile).

Recent work spans wellness DTC (Juice Up), credit union mobile (Allied), GovTech HR/AI (Maia/HRIT), and label e-commerce (URC).

Daniel separates claims by source: Stripe/kitchen tickets for revenue, Vercel Analytics and Microsoft Clarity for web funnel and qualitative friction, store consoles for mobile installs.

Juice Up labels owner-reported lifts (~20% online pickup, ~25% digital base from loyalty migration) and avoids attributing web checkout gains to the app alone. GovTech and banking work emphasizes task completion and adoption narratives with partner context.

Recurring approach: document tokens and components, align Figma with code (including Storybook on Maia), use Radix/shadcn-style primitives for accessible UI, and keep case studies honest about what shipped vs. PoC.

Enterprise / NDA work is shown as diagrams or password-gated prototypes when client UI cannot be public.

Some employer work stays confidential. The portfolio uses anonymized diagrams, outcome framing, and optional password-gated prototypes (e.g. organization admin RBAC) rather than publishing client UI.
